# Diti: the stories first, then the spelling

The marks in **Diti** make the most sense standing next to the myths they have to carry. So the myths come first.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Maruts from the Broken Womb.** The oldest Diti-story has Indra hurl the vajra into her womb, shattering a hundred sons in embryo; the fragments become the Maruts, the storm-gods who yet serve Indra.  Diti’s grief and the storm-gods’ loyalty are the hymn’s tension: the anti-mother’s broken children, adopted by her enemy.

**The Boon of Hiraṇyakaśipu.** Her son Hiraṇyakaśipu, devastated by his brother Hiraṇyākṣa’s death at Varāha’s tusk, won from Brahmā the boon that he could not die by day or night, indoors or out, by man or beast, on earth or sky.  The boon made him lord of the three worlds — until Narasiṃha, the man-lion at dusk on a threshold, ended him.  Diti’s line is the engine of the avatāra cycle.

**The Grandson Who Worshipped the Enemy.** Prahlāda, son of Hiraṇyakaśipu and thus Diti’s grandson, loved Vishnu from the womb — the devotee born in the anti-god’s house.  The Purāṇas make his devotion the theology of bhakti itself: the bound dynasty’s finest fruit was the boy who could not be burned, poisoned, or thrown, for his god held him.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Diti
- **ASCII form:** diti
- **Meaning:** "Daughter of Dakṣa and wife of the sage Kaśyapa, mother of the Daityas, the demon race — the counterpart of her sister Aditi, who is mother of the gods."
- **Domain of influence:** Mother of Demons
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Restoration:** ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** दिति
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 139 of 597

## The Name Travels

Diti is the shadow-twin of Aditi — the Purāṇic genealogists built the whole deva-asura divide from the two sisters’ names.  Her line’s fate — Hiraṇyakaśipu slain, Prahlāda saved — was read by the bhakti commentators as the triumph of devotion over lineage; and modern comparative study pairs her with the bound Titans of Greek genealogy.
